text: That is a maintenance void. The light goes round the room. You, apparently, go into the walls.
The sentries cannot see into the walls. I can. Please remember that.
I held that door open for the test, not for sightseeing. Out you come.
Deliveries go across the acid, not into the wall. I will be updating the labels.
The field resets portals. It does not, it turns out, reset curiosity.
Nothing in this wall is being weighed. Except, from now on, you.
Out there, gravity is a matter of policy. In here, it is a matter of fact. Neither is the test.
You are in the wall again. The sentries have noticed. They are too polite to say.
Those two are out there arguing, and you are in here hiding. I know which of you I respect.
The light is out there. The test is out there. You are, regrettably, in here.
This is not part of the field trip. Nothing in here is educational. Please do not read the walls.
This is the cupboard where I keep the third key. There is no third key. Out.
You are behind the sentry and inside the wall. Two places I specifically did not put a test.
Most subjects who fall off the gantry keep falling. You went into the wall. I am taking notes.
The jump is that way. A long way that way. You have found the one direction I did not mean.
You have rebounded into a wall. That is not a technique I teach.
Catch your breath, by all means. Catch it in the test, where I can see it.
Nothing in this wall moves, crushes or falls. It is the only safe place in the room, which is why it is not in the test.
The plate gives you three seconds. You have chosen to spend them in a wall. Very well.
The test is on the moving panel. This one does not move, and it does not count.
Terminal velocity is reached out there. In here, you have only reached a wall.
